en: While this leopard Kenen was alive,
He struck the Kazakh people once,
He turned them back without letting them face him,
Thinking, Kök came at that moment,
The labor Kökchö had borne,
[Uncertain: the restraint of the dear land,]
[Uncertain: the side of his resentment, lofty barbar,]
Of that land left under a curse.
To the north lay the Kor River,
Who inhabited the Lob River country,
The people wondered whether he would cease fighting,
No soul had turned his attention there,
No living souls had gone there,
Who inhabited that land,
A land that living souls had never seen,
Who had fallen from a mountain like a bay horse,
Of the man who traveled by day,
Whose daily fortune had been cut off,
No solitary man had gone there,
No solitary one remained alive,
Its place was Kenen, its land secure,
From his heart came a tale like this:
An enemy warrior shaped like a man,
There, a man whose back was a mountain,
From where he inhabited the frozen wilderness,
The lone soul who went from captivity,
Did not return alive without dying,
A man stronger than the Creator,
No living man had gone there,
Surambek, khan of the Joygut,
He struck him and drove him back once,
He turned him to face about and returned,
Bringing him safely from Tooz,
His heroism became known,
From the gray-maned prince Kenen,
He made ready as of old,
His assumed name was found,
Was there one in the news of Kere?
Mounted for the mountains and took up his spear,
At home a mace was fastened on,
He struck the one called Künchük,
He turned one back to face him,
Striking Künchük, he took him home,
Destroying the grave, he took the encampment,
Taking a thousand to load the baggage,
Taking the host forward on its march,
Oylok, with fawn-like eyes,
The dark-eyed one he had in mind,
Would he speak of the crimson dress?
He seized and tore away their possessions,
Throwing them into distress, he raged,
He turned one back to face him,
The hero's heroic strength became known,
No enemy could remain before his advance,
Nothing remained in the treasury to give,
Those who saw this lost heart,
Saying, 'This ill-omened Kenen,'
Saying, 'This is the bloodthirsty hero's son,'
Despairing before his power,
His charge left them wounded,
They cried out before him,
If you observe him, this Kenen is formidable,
Saying, 'No man will go and face him,'
Saying, 'Whoever meets him will not remain standing,'
Those who fought him fell back defeated,
Saying, 'There is no strength to make him yield,'
To his right lay the Russian people,
They thought, 'So this is Kenen,'
His might was as fierce as China's wrath,
Saying, 'If you grapple with him, ready your life,'
So the Russian people thought,
Before them stood a firearm,
These wretched ones were of the Kyrgyz tribe,
Intending to overrun and oppress them,
A countless host gathered from the rich lords,
They came saying, “We will wage war,”
Barak's banner was brought down,
With Ebegey and Kögöy there as well,
Kenen became lord over these Kyrgyz,
This assembled army was scattered,
This hero's people were subdued,
The people of this foe faltered,
Those Kalmyk souls who said they would do battle,
Those fierce warriors who would wage holy war,
Their great stronghold was cut down,
Their great ambition was checked,
Their forefather was Khan Tugan,
From the beginning, the line had continued one by one,
There was no regret in what she had received,
One of the seven days brings death,
For God will take every person,
The cold-bosomed black earth,
Will one day open its embrace,
A soul is but a guest for seven days,
And will return when its turn comes,
The cold-bosomed black earth,
Will one day draw us to its bosom,
No person has a breast of iron,
Even a cherished noble soul,
Will return when the children come of age,
Her platter-round face brightened,
Thinking her dear sister-in-law would take them,
The deep-rooted black earth,
Will one day open its embrace,
Stirring the people and gathering the nation,
Those who did not hold back rejoiced,
His honor, fortune, and prosperity,
Became known to the multitude,
Such was the hero Kenen,
The four kinds of livestock stood ready,
May God never let us see such a sight,
The multitude standing there came to a halt,
An ancestral household that would never be exhausted,
People filled the face of the earth,
They held the feast for seven days,
The warrior restrained the fierce ones,
It made the lower-ranking men rejoice,
It made those in the encampment crane their necks proudly,
Its two humps rose prominently,
Dust covered its forehead,
It planted all four feet evenly,
Dust covered its shaggy hair,
The black camel glared fiercely,
The camel, lord among livestock,
Looking like a thoroughbred camel,
He had all of it loaded onto camels,
He held equestrian entertainments,
Having the black load piled on,
They say he held a great feast,
Seeking a means to beguile them,
Livestock gathered in countless numbers,
For the people who remained alive,
Their hearts were truly put at ease,
Two treasures' worth of white sheep,
Having their lambs slaughtered,
Leaving their mothers in the dark,
Precious goods were gathered among them,
Slaughtering mares amid the bustle,
For it, slaughtering three hump-backed camels,
The dark livestock of all four kinds,
Slaughtering equally from all four kinds of livestock,
Yellow gold piled in abundance,
They say he proclaimed its worth imploringly,
Today, countless livestock for the household,
They say he scattered its share lavishly,
Of every person who came,
They say he attended even to the last of them,
For all of them, and for the poor,
